title: Aft Cargo Door Structure — Stringer Splice Repair at the Cut-Out Corner
abstract: Permanent splice repair for a cracked or damaged stringer at the aft cargo door cut-out corner, restoring the load path into the surrounding frame without removing the door surround splice plates.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the axial load path of a cargo door structure stringer that has cracked or been damaged at the cut-out corner, using a splice that is installed from inside the compartment without disturbing the surround splice plates.
sections.damage_assessment: Establish the extent of the damage by detailed visual inspection with the door removed and the local lining stripped. Measure the crack length along the stringer flange and record its distance from the corner radius. Damage confined to one flange may be repaired by this scheme; damage that crosses the web, that reaches the corner radius itself, or that is accompanied by any deformation of the surround, is outside the scope and requires an engineering assessment. Check whether the aircraft carries the reinforced surround standard, because the splice fastener pattern is different for each and the wrong pattern will fall inside the edge distance of the surround plate.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the aft cargo door and strip the lining local to the corner. Cut out the damaged length of stringer to the limits given on repair drawing RD-52-30-11-904, leaving a straight cut normal to the flange at each end. Do a dye penetrant inspection of both cut faces. Prepare the splice from the stock given on sheet 1 and check its fit dry against the remaining stringer ends. Apply the chromate-free surface protection to all bare metal. Where the aircraft carries the reinforced surround, use the offset fastener pattern on sheet 2; otherwise use the pattern on sheet 1. Install the splice wet with sealant using the blind rivets AGS534950-40 and, at the outboard end, the angle JA880258-89 to carry the load into the frame. Refit the edging grommet AES686504-33 where the wiring route crosses the new fastener line. Install the door, rig it and measure the closing effort before the lining is restored.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is not life limited but carries a repeat detailed visual inspection of the splice and of the corner radius at every C check, and an eddy current inspection of the outer fastener row every 8000 flight cycles. Any indication at the splice, or a measured closing effort outside the published limit at any subsequent check, makes the repair invalid. Report the repair to Aeralis with the crack length and position so that it is recorded against the aircraft.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Damage confined to one stringer flange over a length not exceeding 90 millimetres, not reaching the cut-out corner radius and with no measurable deformation of the door surround.

repair_drawings.title: Stringer splice, aft cargo door cut-out corner

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two rows of 24 blind rivets AGS534950-40, 18 mm pitch, 12 mm edge distance; offset pattern on reinforced surround aircraft
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Not life limited; repeat detailed visual at every C check and eddy current inspection of the outer fastener row every 8000 flight cycles.
